:::{#thm-entropy-chain-rule}
#### Chain rule for entropy

For discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$,

$$H(X, Y) = H(X) + H(Y \mid X).$$

:::

::: {.proof}

Use the notation of @def-conditional-entropy,
with every sum over the pairs with $p(x, y) > 0$.
Since $p(x, y) = p(x) \, p(y \mid x)$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
H(X, Y)
&= -\sum_{x, y} p(x, y) \log p(x, y) \\
&= -\sum_{x, y} p(x, y) \log \sb{p(x) \, p(y \mid x)} \\
&= -\sum_{x, y} p(x, y) \log p(x)
   - \sum_{x, y} p(x, y) \log p(y \mid x) \\
&= -\sum_{x} \log p(x) \sum_{y} p(x, y)
   - \sum_{x} p(x) \sum_{y} p(y \mid x) \log p(y \mid x) \\
&= -\sum_{x} p(x) \log p(x)
   + \sum_{x} p(x) \, H(Y \mid X=x) \\
&= H(X) + H(Y \mid X).
\end{aligned}
$$

The fourth line groups the terms by $x$
and uses $p(x, y) = p(x) \, p(y \mid x)$ in the second sum;
the fifth uses $\sum_{y} p(x, y) = p(x)$ and the definition of $H(Y \mid X=x)$.

:::
